The explicit dependency on the managed node-group IAM role duplicates the implicit dependency from node_role_arn (aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn).
The null resource interpolates the IAM role ID in its local-exec command, already establishing an implicit dependency on this role; the explicit depends_on entry is duplicative.
The null resource interpolates the Spark namespace ID in its local-exec command, already establishing an implicit dependency on this namespace; the explicit depends_on entry is duplicative.

This ASG already depends transitively on the IAM role through its launch-template input, which references the instance profile and that profile references the role. The direct explicit role dependency adds no ordering.
The ASG already depends on this instance profile through its launch-template input/output chain, so the direct explicit dependency is duplicative.
The aws-auth ConfigMap already waits for the EKS readiness data source, which itself depends on the EKS cluster module; the additional direct dependency on the cluster module is redundant.
The VPC CNI ConfigMap already waits for the EKS readiness data source, which itself depends on the EKS cluster module; the additional direct dependency on the cluster module is redundant.

The stateful example enables EKS managed node groups but does not pass their ARN through data_plane_wait_arn or otherwise order Kubernetes add-on deployment after the managed node group. Add-ons may begin before worker nodes are available, affecting workload scheduling and data-plane-dependent add-ons.

The Velero Helm chart deploys pods, but the example add-ons module has no ordering edge to the managed node group. With Terraform applying these concurrently, Helm may wait or time out while the cluster has no schedulable worker nodes.

The EFS CSI Helm release deploys controller workloads and may be installed before the example's managed node group is available, leaving its pods pending and potentially causing Helm's readiness wait to fail.

The self-managed EBS CSI Helm release deploys controller workloads, but no dependency orders it after the managed node group. Installing it before worker nodes become available can leave Helm waiting for unschedulable pods.
